title: Unlocking Teacher Agency for Professional Learning Through Connection-Building: Evidence from a Professional Development Program on China’s Standards of English Language Ability
body_coverage: Full Introduction, Literature Review, Research Methods, three Findings case narratives, Discussion and Conclusion/limitations. Table 1 read; no diagram-only propositions used. References not individually retraced.
design: Nine voluntary teachers in an eight-session CSE professional-development program at an East-China university subsidiary college, followed by two-month consultation availability. Three successful/insightful key informants selected by engagement, continuing effort and project progress; Chinese recordings/reflections, artefacts and 51–69-minute interviews. First author was program instructor/guest professor.
parse_check: Native section and paragraph order inspected. Claims here use body narratives, not uninspected diagram features. Authors' mapping of ownership onto subject/object versus subject/tool connections is not internally clear; retain the concrete actions instead of silently repairing their framework labels. Table 1 confirms three female lecturers with M.A. qualifications, 6–12 years teaching; table inspected, no new population inference.

moves.problem: A list of PD features does not explain how a common tool becomes useful for different teachers.
locations: Findings:Mary, Zoe and Peggy case narratives
moves.author_move: Mary uses CSE descriptors to specify objectives for a tourism course, Zoe for teaching-competition lesson design, Peggy for proficiency selection/measurement in a doctoral proposal. The discussion compares goals, knowledge and application rather than simply calling all three teachers motivated.
moves.project_inference: Use contrasting practical purposes to show what a shared process has in common and what must remain specific. Move from an abstract property such as agency to the actions and unresolved task difficulties it describes.
moves.condition: These are three selected success cases. No comparison of all nine teachers' agency change or alternative mechanisms is demonstrated.

moves.problem: The introduction's explanatory gap disappears behind a final contribution label.
locations: Literature Review:Teacher Agency for Professional Learning
Literature Review:Understanding Teacher Agency from an Activity Theory Perspective
moves.author_move: Starts from existing descriptions of supportive PD features and systemic tensions, then examines teachers' work connecting a standard to professional goals; returns to that shift when describing an agency-oriented approach.
moves.project_inference: State the specific additional relation that the findings make visible, rather than claim theoretical extension merely by adding a new label.
moves.condition: Application difficulties remain (e.g. adapting general descriptors to tourism). Do not write successful use as complete resolution or long-term sustainable growth.

do_not_adopt: Success-selected informants cannot establish that this program unlocks agency generally or is more effective than alternatives.
Career advancement pressures and instrument-specific expertise are context, not generic learner motivation.
Winning a competition or defending a proposal is reported progress; the design does not isolate the program as its cause.
Positive attitudes, ownership and application should not be treated as measured interchangeable components of agency.
The instructor's ongoing relationships are both context/rapport and a potential influence on accounts, not a guarantee of reliability.
